## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-dsc-definition

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2: definition of historical DSC, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-dsc-ratio

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15 (7(a) Changes of Ownership), Para. C.2: debt service coverage, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** For a 7(a) change of ownership, the lender tests debt service coverage on the last fiscal year-end or the average of the last two, at 1.25:1 for an initial acquisition or owner buyout and 1.15:1 for a business expansion.
- **Quote:** "The Debt Service Coverage (DSC) ratio must be satisfied using either the last fiscal year-end or an average of the last two fiscal year-end statements on either a historical or adjusted basis based on the transaction type: Initial Acquisition: 1.25:1 Business Expansion: 1.15:1 Owner Buyout: 1.25:1 ESOP and Cooperative: 1.25:1"
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-qualified-source

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: qualified source for business valuations, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** An SBA business valuation must come from an accredited, independent valuation professional with no conflict of interest.
- **Quote:** "A “Qualified Source” is an individual who regularly receives compensation for business valuations and is accredited by one of the following recognized organizations and is independent of the loan production function, not involved in the approval of the transaction, and must not have the appearance of a conflict of interest:"
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-real-estate-structure

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: real estate in an acquisition, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** When an SBA acquisition loan also buys real estate, only the real estate portion may amortize longer than 10 years, up to 25; everything else gets 10 years.
- **Quote:** "Only the portion of the real estate purchase may have an amortization that exceeds 10-years, up to a maximum of a 25-year term. All other uses of proceeds, including those related to soft costs and working capital, must be allocated a 10-year term."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-seller-consultant

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: seller may stay only as a consultant, up to 24 months, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** In an SBA 7(a) initial acquisition or business expansion, the seller can't stay as an officer, director, owner or employee, but the business may hire the seller as a consultant for up to 24 months in total.
- **Quote:** "Except as provided below, the seller in a Business Expansion or Initial Acquisition change of ownership transaction may not remain as an officer, director, stockholder, or employee of the business. If a transitional period is needed to assist the business, the small business may contract with the seller as a consultant for a period not to exceed 24 months (in aggregate, including any extensions)."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-seller-debt-equity

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: seller debt as equity, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Seller debt counts as equity for SBA purposes only if it is subordinated and on full standby, with no principal or interest payments for the life of the 7(a) loan.
- **Quote:** "Seller debt that is subordinated to the Lender and on full standby (no payments of principal or interest for the term of the 7(a) loan) may be considered as equity for SBA’s purposes."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-seller-note-refi-terms

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: conditions to refinance a seller note, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** A seller note can be refinanced with SBA financing only after 36 months in place and current, and the refinancing must improve the payment by at least 10 percent.
- **Quote:** "To be eligible for refinancing, any seller-financed Note must have been in place and current (not on standby) for at least 36 months following the change of ownership. The refinancing request must meet the SBA’s 10 percent improvement to installment payment amount requirement and must not reduce the Lender's exposure."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-seller-rebate-principal

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: seller rebates go to principal, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** A rebate the buyer receives from the seller must be used to pay down the 7(a) loan that funded the purchase.
- **Quote:** "If the Borrower receives funds based on a rebate from the seller, proceeds must be applied to pay down the principal balance of the 7(a) loan that funded the change of ownership."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-spouse-guaranty

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. A: guaranty of spouse, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** A spouse owning under 20% must guarantee in full when spouses and minor children together own 20% or more.
- **Quote:** "Each spouse owning less than 20% of an Applicant must personally guarantee the loan in full when the combined ownership interest of both spouses and minor children is 20% or more."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-standby-terms

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2.a: standby debt agreements, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Standby debt may accrue interest to be paid after the 7(a) loan is repaid, and the standby creditor must subordinate its liens and take no action without the lender’s consent.
- **Quote:** "The standby debt may accrue interest and may be added to the standby debt and amortized after the 7(a) loan is paid in full. Standby Creditor must subordinate any lien rights in collateral securing the loan to Lender’s rights in the collateral and take no action against Borrower or any collateral securing the Standby Debt without Lender’s consent."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-three-years

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2.b: three years of financials, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** The lender analyzes the three most recent year-ends of the acquired business.
- **Quote:** "For acquired business, and for Applicants that are an existing operating entity, the Lender’s financial analysis must be based on the three most recent year-end historical financial information using the highest level of financial reporting available."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-total-debt-cap

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: total debt limited to the valuation, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** All debt in an SBA acquisition, including seller debt not on full standby, is capped at the business valuation and must be covered by cash flow.
- **Quote:** "The total debt eligible to support a change of ownership transaction (including seller debt that is not on full standby) is limited to the business valuation amount and must be supported by the Debt Service Coverage of the Applicant."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-transferable-licenses

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: transferable licenses as collateral, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** In an SBA change of ownership, the lender must take as collateral all assets conveyed, including transferable licenses such as a liquor license.
- **Quote:** "With the exception of vehicles as described in Para. C.3.d.i., evidence that all assets, including transferable licenses (e.g., liquor license) conveyed as a result of purchase are properly secured as collateral by Lender."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-valuation-350k

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: lender may value deals of $350,000 or less, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** For a business purchase price of $350,000 or less, the lender may do its own valuation instead of using an outside qualified source, unless buyer and seller are closely related.
- **Quote:** "If the Business Purchase Price is $350,000 or less, the Lender may perform its own valuation of the business being sold, unless there is a close relationship between the buyer and seller."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-valuation-for-lender

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: business valuation prepared for the lender, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** The SBA business valuation must be ordered by and prepared for the lender; one prepared for the buyer or seller can't be used.
- **Quote:** "For the individual performing the business valuation to identify the scope of work appropriately, the business valuation must be requested by and prepared for the Lender. The Lender may not use a business valuation prepared for the Applicant or the seller."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-valuation-gap-equity

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: price above valuation is covered by equity, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** If the price is higher than the independent business valuation, the difference must come from equity, not more debt.
- **Quote:** "The business valuation must support the Business Purchase Price as defined in Paragraph A.1 regardless of how the debt is structured. If the amount paid for the business exceeds the business valuation, the difference must be made up by equity."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-working-assets-line

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: working assets on a line of credit, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** A lender may finance the part of the purchase that relates to working assets (such as receivables and inventory) on a line of credit.
- **Quote:** "Lenders may fund a portion of the purchase related to the working assets of the firm onto a line of credit as outlined in Section C. Para. 3.d.i.e of this Appendix."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-working-capital-adequacy

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: working capital adequacy, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** For an acquisition loan the lender analyzes whether working capital is adequate for at least the next 12 months.
- **Quote:** "Analysis of working capital adequacy, at a minimum, over the next 12 months;"
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26
